_comment: Module 5 (Simulink screening-throughput) input parameters. Owned by R3 (Abhigyat), consumed by R4 (Natik). Every parameter carries a 'confidence' tag: SOURCED = read from a cited primary source; DERIVED = computed from a sourced figure or from our own measured dataset; ASSUMED = a placeholder we chose, NOT evidence. The README risk table names unrealistic assumptions as a headline project risk - so ASSUMED values must appear as assumptions in the Phase 5 write-up, never as findings. Reasoning and citations: docs/telemedicine_parameters.md

target_patients_per_year.source: SIH problem statement - district-scale rollout target

operating_days_per_year.note: 6-day week less public holidays. Drives everything downstream - vary it in scenario analysis.

images_per_patient.source: Dey et al. 2025 (AIDRSS, Kolkata): 5,029 participants, 10,058 macula-centric images
images_per_patient.note: One macula-centric field per eye. A 2-field protocol would double this.

arrival_process.note: Walk-in screening camps are bursty, not Poisson. If SimEvents allows, test a batch-arrival variant - camps deliver 40-60 patients in a morning, which changes queue depth far more than the mean rate does.

technician_time_per_patient_min.note: Registration + positioning + two captures + retry. NOT sourced - the single most valuable parameter for R3 to replace with a real time-and-motion figure.

vision_centre_catchment_population.source: Aravind Eye Care System vision centre model

vision_centre_catchment_radius_km.source: Aravind Eye Care System vision centre model

staff_per_centre.source: Aravind / LVPEI vision centre staffing model; technicians receive 2 years training plus 1 year supervision

image_size_mb.note: Placeholder for a 4288x2848 JPEG (IDRiD's uniform resolution). REPLACE WITH A MEASUREMENT - once IDRiD is on a machine this is a one-liner; see docs/telemedicine_parameters.md section 4.

national_avg_fixed_broadband_download_mb.note: NATIONAL average, download. Not a rural PHC figure and not an upload figure - do not model with this directly.

assumed_rural_phc_upload_mbps.note: Upload is the binding constraint and no rural upload figure was found. Treat as a scenario axis, not a constant: sweep 1 / 5 / 20 Mbps and report where upload stops being the bottleneck.

connectivity_fallback.source: Indian teleophthalmology deployments historically used VSAT (ISRO) satellite links for rural image transfer
connectivity_fallback.note: Model a store-and-forward path - images queue locally and sync in batches. This makes the system robust to an outage rather than dependent on live bandwidth, and is the realistic rural design.

inference_time_per_image_s.statistic: MEAN - deliberately, not the median. See why_mean_not_median.
inference_time_per_image_s.source: simulink/benchmarkInferenceTime.m, n=18 IDRiD images (2 warm-up discarded), MATLAB R2026a, CPU

distribution.shape: Right-skewed and near-bimodal: ~two thirds of images run 6.8-8.3 s, ~one third run 13-25 s. The slow set is reproducible - the same images are slow in every run - so it is image content, not measurement noise.

inference_time_per_image_s.why_mean_not_median: A queueing model's service time is an EXPECTATION: throughput is total work over time, so the mean is the correct statistic. An earlier revision of this entry used the median (7.65 s), which under-states the compute requirement by ~39% on this distribution. The median is the right number for answering 'how long does a typical image take'; it is the wrong number for sizing a compute node.
inference_time_per_image_s.cold_start_note: The FIRST image of a MATLAB session costs ~16-25 s (model load, BLAS/JIT warm-up). Warm-up images are excluded from these statistics. A long-running service pays this once; a per-invocation script pays it every time.
inference_time_per_image_s.device_note: CPU. explainGrading.m builds a plain CPU dlarray, so predict() runs on the CPU even with a GPU present. Measured: CNN forward CPU 0.050 s vs GPU 0.034 s; forward+Grad-CAM CPU 0.514 s vs GPU 0.732 s (GPU SLOWER - transfer overhead exceeds compute at this model size).
inference_time_per_image_s.deployment_implication: A PHC edge node does NOT need a GPU: the pipeline is CPU-bound in classical CV, and moving the CNN to a GPU would save ~0.016 s of ~10.6 s. Report generation is negligible (0.21 s).

quality_reject_rate.source: Dey et al. 2025 (AIDRSS): 547/5,029 (10.9%) excluded for image quality - poor illumination, motion artifacts

idx_dr_field_imageability.source: Abramoff et al. 2018 - 96.1% imageability in the FDA pivotal trial

quality_reject_rate.note: KEY MODELLING INSIGHT: field reject rates (3.9-10.9%) are 20-60x the curated-dataset rate (0.2%). Module 5 must model a RECAPTURE LOOP - a rejected image sends the patient back to acquisition, not out of the system. Ignoring it understates technician load by ~10%.

ophthalmologist_review_time_s.status: UNVALIDATED - no clinician has been timed
ophthalmologist_review_time_s.note: This is our Module 4 DESIGN TARGET, not an observed figure. Using it as a model input makes every throughput result conditional on Module 4 hitting that target - state that.

measured_counter_evidence.source: src/explainability/usabilityPass.m - critical path of the rendered report is ~126 words; 38 s is that at 200 wpm silent reading
measured_counter_evidence.what_it_is: A FLOOR on reading alone: it assumes the reviewer reads each word once, looks at no image, and makes no judgement. A real review also inspects the Grad-CAM overlay against the evidence table, which is the slow part and is NOT included.
measured_counter_evidence.implication: The measured floor (38 s) is ALREADY ABOVE the assumed review time (30 s). If anything this assumption is OPTIMISTIC, so specialist-load figures in docs/phase5_results.md section 5 are more likely under-estimates than over-estimates. Do not treat 30 s as conservative.

ophthalmologist_review_time_s.to_close: Sit a clinician in front of reports/usability/index.html with a stopwatch. The review set and protocol are already generated by usabilityPass.m. Until then every staffing number derived from this value is unvalidated.

referral_rate.source: Dey et al. 2025 (AIDRSS) severity breakdown: DR2 4.40% + DR3/DR4 0.14%, recomputed against OUR referable definition (ICDR >= 2)
referral_rate.note: The paper's own headline 'referable' rate is 0.14% because it counts only DR3-DR4. Recomputed here for ICDR >= 2. DME-only referrals are NOT included - so this is a floor. See docs/clinical_definitions.md section 3.

dr_prevalence_general_population.source: Dey et al. 2025 (AIDRSS), Kolkata, n=4,482 gradable (95% CI 12.6-14.8%)

comparator.source: SMART India, Lancet Global Health 2022 (95% CI 11.0-14.2%)

dr_prevalence_elevated_blood_glucose.note: Scenario lever: screening a diabetic-only cohort roughly triples yield per image and changes the optimal staffing mix.

referred_onward_to_base_hospital.source: Aravind Eye Care System: 'over 90% can be fully treated on-site and less than 10% are referred to the base hospital'
referred_onward_to_base_hospital.note: Second-stage referral, downstream of our AI decision. Relevant to the district capacity claim, not to image throughput.

ophthalmologists_per_million_india.source: Online Journal of Public Health Informatics 2024;16:e50921 (South India workforce survey), doi:10.2196/50921
ophthalmologists_per_million_india.note: Read from the abstract via search; full text was not retrievable (publisher returned empty body). VERIFY BEFORE SLIDE USE.

district_ratio_range.note: This 30x within-state spread is a stronger argument for the project than any national average. See docs/telemedicine_parameters.md section 5.
